reason: The cited evidence does not address HfZrTiTa0.53 or any thermomechanical processing of it. E1 shows tensile ductility in a different annealed alloy, E2 reports only compressive properties, and E3 concerns a different composition and loading modes. None of the key premises about the proposed intervention, mechanism, or preservation of energy release are supported by the cited passages.
premises: Cold rolling and annealing can refine grain structure in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Grain refinement increases grain boundary area, promoting dislocation activity and uniform plasticity.
Controlled annealing can limit strength loss while improving ductility.
Impact-triggered energy release is preserved after thermomechanical processing.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has limited tensile ductility in the as-cast state.
